recommendation: Keep the core audit commit. If requirements-parent needs correction, migration, or a root-level context change, handle it in HL7/fhir-extensions or through a new FHIR-I decision rather than adding an unapproved root Requirements.parent element in this core reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-39059 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Requirements. It requested a parent relationship to organize Requirements hierarchically and the final resolution text asked for a 0..1 Requirements.parent string with a convention similar to statement.derivedFrom.
initial_application: Core commit 9e8dc87830 applied the request as Requirements.statement.parent. Jira follow-up comments said this was one level lower than intended, and Lloyd McKenzie then noted the change could not be completed in core and pointed to the Extension Pack requirements-parent extension added by e38fb3c.
additional_context: Requirements is active in the current core build. The current StructureDefinition has no root Requirements.parent; it has the later R6 statement-level relation model, including Requirements.statement.partOf with reference/key children. FHIR-47739 and FHIR-47736, already represented on the combined branch, renamed statement.parent to statement.partOf, clarified derivedFrom versus partOf, and completed the current partOf representation.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. The reconciliation published an external-repo audit because adding a root Requirements.parent now would be a new unapproved core change and would ignore the Extension Pack handoff and later R6 relation decisions.

related_jiras.note: Renamed Requirements.statement.parent to Requirements.statement.partOf and clarified the statement-level hierarchy semantics now present in R6 core.
Completed the current statement relation representation by splitting partOf/derivedFrom into reference/key children and making partOf repeatable.
